summary:
COSMIC FRONTIER: Mission Survival is a browser-based educational space survival 
simulation designed for children aged 7–12. Players become commanders of a 
NASA-inspired lunar or Martian research outpost, managing oxygen, energy, food, 
water, radiation shielding, and crew health across a multi-day mission.

The game features a dynamic decision engine with 15+ scientifically grounded 
mission events — each presenting three choices with real resource costs and 
consequences. Players discover that every decision ripples across all systems: 
growing food needs water and energy; stronger shielding costs materials and power; 
research burns electricity.

Authentic NASA data is integrated throughout: live solar weather from the NASA 
DONKI API influences in-game radiation events, real Mars Rover photographs appear 
during gameplay, and NASA OSDR astronaut health findings are shown as science facts. 
A simulated Mars communication delay mechanic teaches children about the speed of 
light across planetary distances.

The game is fully free, requires no login or download, and runs in any browser at 
https://adorable-naiad-5a0c36.netlify.app
details:
WHAT WE BUILT

COSMIC FRONTIER: Mission Survival is an interactive educational survival game

that places children in command of a real NASA-style mission. Players must keep

their astronaut crew alive by making smart resource management decisions every

mission day — experiencing firsthand the complexity and consequence of space

exploration.

HOW IT WORKS

Players choose one of two missions:

- Lunar Outpost: Survive 10 days on the Moon's south polar region. Key threats:

radiation exposure and power management during the lunar night.

- Mars Outpost: Survive 30 sols on Mars. Key threats: dust storms cutting solar

power, oxygen production delays, food scarcity, and communication lag.

Each day, a randomized mission event presents a crisis with three possible

responses. Every choice has resource costs (energy, materials, oxygen, time) and

visible consequences. After each decision, the game explains the real science

behind the outcome in child-friendly language.

RESOURCE SIMULATION ENGINE

A configurable simulation engine runs every mission day, calculating:

- Oxygen consumption and life-support replenishment rates

- Solar energy generation (reduced during dust storms or low-sun conditions)

- Food and water consumption and greenhouse production timelines

- Radiation exposure based on shielding level and solar events

- Crew health and fatigue from resource shortfalls

Resources are genuinely interdependent — not isolated sliders. This models real

closed-loop life-support systems aboard actual space habitats.

MARS COMMUNICATION DELAY MECHANIC

When a player contacts Earth for advice, the game simulates the signal travel

time between planets. A countdown runs, then Mission Control responds — teaching

children that Mars is 4 to 24 light-minutes away depending on orbital position.

NASA SCIENCE LAB SCREEN

A dedicated Science Lab screen lets players explore deeper space science through

real NASA research findings from OSDR (astronaut bone density, muscle changes,

sleep disruption, immune response in microgravity) and live solar weather data

from the DONKI API.

EDUCATIONAL OUTCOMES

Children who play COSMIC FRONTIER develop:

- Systems thinking: understanding that resources are interconnected

- Consequence awareness: every trade-off has a downstream effect

- Space science literacy: real NASA concepts experienced through gameplay

- Critical thinking under pressure: evaluating three options with limited time

TECHNICAL IMPLEMENTATION

The game is built with React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion,

Recharts, and the NASA Open APIs. It is deployed on Netlify with global HTTPS.

No login, no download, and no installation is required. Progress is auto-saved

to localStorage. The app is fully responsive across desktop, tablet, and mobile.
